# server

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/server"
```

Package server — the two group options only an HTTP group reads: the header phase's own deadline and the header size cap.

Package server is the inbound half of the SDK's network domain (ADR 0029): one unified listener engine for TCP, Unix, TLS and mutual TLS, serving pluggable handlers grouped behind shared middlewares.

### The whole thing

```
srv := server.New()
srv.Group("echo", server.Listen("tcp", ":8080")).
	HandleFunc(func(ctx context.Context, c server.Conn) error {
		_, err := io.Copy(c, c)
		return err
	})
err := srv.Serve(ctx)
```

That is the design target, not a simplified excerpt. [Conn](#Conn) embeds net.Conn, so a handler reads and writes a connection exactly as it would any socket and every io helper keeps working — io.Copy, bufio, encoding wrappers. Everything the domain adds is additive.

### Groups

A group is a set of listeners sharing one handler, one middleware chain and one policy. It exists so the same handler can answer on a TCP port and a Unix socket without wiring it twice:

```
srv.Group("api",
	server.Listen("tcp", ":8443"),
	server.Listen("unix", "/run/api.sock"),
	server.TLS(identity),
	server.IdleTimeout(30*time.Second),
).Use(mw).Handle(handler)
```

[Group](#Group) returns the group rather than a (group, error) pair on purpose: a declaration mistake — a duplicate name, an unusable address, a missing handler — is recorded and reported by [Server](#Server).Start. The declaration chain stays readable, and nothing is swallowed.

### TLS and mutual TLS

One option covers both. A [github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/tlsid.Identity](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/tlsid#Identity) built with RequireClientCert turns the group's listeners into mutual-TLS listeners; the same identity type serves the outbound client, so the two cannot drift apart. The handshake runs on the connection's own goroutine, so a slow or hostile peer cannot stall the accept path for everyone else.

### Lifecycle

[Server](#Server).Start returns once every listener is bound, so a nil error means the ports are open. [Server](#Server).Serve starts, blocks until the context is cancelled, then drains. [Server](#Server).Shutdown stops accepting and waits for in-flight work within a budget, severing what remains when the budget expires — a shutdown that never returns is worse than one that admits it gave up.

[Server](#Server).State reports the phase, the addresses actually bound, and whether any listener fell back from a requested optimisation. A silent degradation is indistinguishable from a working server, so it is surfaced rather than logged once at startup.

An Accept that fails for any reason but its listener closing — the process out of file descriptors, typically — is retried after a wait, never at once: 5 ms, doubling, held at one second, started over by the next accepted connection, as net/http's own Serve does. Retrying at once would spin a core per listener for as long as the condition lasts. A shutdown during a wait ends it at once, and [State](#State).AcceptBackoffs counts the waits, so a server that cannot accept says so.

### Connections that never end

A drain waits for in-flight work to finish, which assumes it eventually does. An event stream, a long poll, or anything built on a protocol upgrade breaks that assumption: the request is in flight forever by design, so the drain waits out its whole budget and then severs the socket under the handler.

[DrainSignal](#DrainSignal) is the way out. A handler holding a connection open selects on it alongside its own work and returns when it closes, which turns a budget-length DRAIN\_TIMEOUT into a clean drain:

```
select {
case <-server.DrainSignal(r.Context()):
	return
case ev := <-events:
	// …
}
```

The request context is deliberately NOT cancelled to say this. Cancelling it would tell every handler to abandon the response it is halfway through, which is the opposite of what a graceful drain is for. The signal is additive: a handler that ignores it behaves exactly as it did before.

[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/sse](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/sse) is the Server-Sent Events implementation built on it, and watches the signal for you.

### Protocol upgrades

[github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/websocket](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/net/websocket) is WebSocket (RFC 6455), server side. It hijacks the response, which means the socket stops being the engine's: it is neither closed nor waited for by a drain — the same carve-out http.Server.Shutdown documents for hijacked connections. The connection watches [DrainSignal](#DrainSignal) and closes itself with a 1001 "going away" instead, so a deployment ends it deliberately rather than by severing it.

The same is true of anything else a handler hijacks: once the socket is taken over it is the handler's to close.

<a name="Adopt"></a>
## func [Adopt](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Adopt(names ...string) GroupOption
```

Adopt takes over a socket inherited from a supervisor instead of binding one.

Socket activation is what makes a zero-downtime restart possible: the supervisor holds the bound socket across the exec, so no connection is lost and no bind races. The name is the one the unit file publishes in LISTEN\_FDNAMES. Repeat the option to adopt several sockets into one group.

A named socket the supervisor did not pass is SocketAdoptFailed, never a silent fallback to binding: a service that quietly binds its own port has lost exactly the property activation exists to provide. The same holds on Windows, which has no socket activation at all: Start fails there with SocketAdoptFailed, whose cause field names UNSUPPORTED\_PLATFORM.

<a name="BatchSize"></a>
## func [BatchSize](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func BatchSize(n int) GroupOption
```

BatchSize sets how many datagrams one read attempts to collect. One disables batching; zero selects the platform default. Where the platform cannot batch, State reports the degradation rather than hiding it.

<a name="Chain"></a>
## func [Chain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Chain(h Handler, middlewares ...Middleware) Handler
```

Chain applies middlewares to a handler, outermost first.

Chain(h, a, b, c) yields a(b(c(h))): the first middleware listed is the first to see a connection, matching how the list reads at the call site.

<a name="ChainPacket"></a>
## func [ChainPacket](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func ChainPacket(h PacketHandler, middlewares ...PacketMiddleware) PacketHandler
```

ChainPacket applies middlewares to a datagram handler, outermost first.

<a name="DrainSignal"></a>
## func [DrainSignal](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func DrainSignal(ctx context.Context) <-chan struct{}
```

DrainSignal returns the channel closed when the server serving this request begins draining, or nil when none is published.

It is how a handler that holds a connection open indefinitely — an event stream, a long poll — learns that finishing now is the cooperative thing to do. Without it such a handler holds the drain open until the budget expires and its socket is severed under it, on every shutdown.

A nil channel blocks forever, so a select that watches it needs no nil check and behaves correctly on a server that publishes nothing.

<a name="Engine"></a>
## func [Engine](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Engine(e EngineValue) GroupOption
```

Engine names the engine family the group runs on: EngineGoroutine, one goroutine per connection, or EngineLoop, the loop engine; Loop then picks the loop's backend. The zero value, EngineAuto, lets the handler's type choose. An engine the group's handler cannot run on, or that another option contradicts — EngineGoroutine with Loop or HandleLoop, EngineLoop with Handle, HandleFunc or HandleHTTP or on a datagram group — fails Start with EngineUnsupported, and is never replaced by the other engine.

<a name="HandshakeTimeout"></a>
## func [HandshakeTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func HandshakeTimeout(d time.Duration) GroupOption
```

HandshakeTimeout bounds the TLS negotiation on the group's listeners.

Unset does not mean unbounded, unlike the other three. The handshake runs on the connection's own goroutine — the listener does not negotiate in Accept, which is what keeps one slow peer from stalling the accept path for everyone — so it is the one phase that can be stalled before any handler exists to notice, and a peer that connects and says nothing would otherwise hold a goroutine and a slot under MaxConns indefinitely. It falls back to a domain default instead.

<a name="IdleTimeout"></a>
## func [IdleTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func IdleTimeout(d time.Duration) GroupOption
```

IdleTimeout bounds how long a connection may sit with no traffic at all.

It is enforced on the read side, where silence is observable: a read is bounded by whichever of ReadTimeout and IdleTimeout is tighter. Setting both therefore narrows the bound rather than replacing it, which is what the two options together are asking for.

<a name="Listen"></a>
## func [Listen](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Listen(network string, addr string) GroupOption
```

Listen adds an address to a group. Repeat it to bind several addresses to one handler — a TCP port and a Unix socket, for instance.

On Windows, whose AF\_UNIX sockets are stream-only, a "unixgram" or "unixpacket" address fails Start with the SDK's UNSUPPORTED\_PLATFORM, before any socket is opened; "unix" is served there as everywhere else.

<a name="Loop"></a>
## func [Loop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Loop(v LoopValue) GroupOption
```

Loop configures a group's loop engine (ADR 0186 §D5): its backend, its loops and rings, and its per-connection and pressure bounds. It is judged at Start, once the group's handler is known: a group served by HandleLoop runs on it, and a group served by Handle, HandleFunc or HandleHTTP refuses it with LoopOptionUnsupported, whichever order the declarations came in. A group with no handler fails with HandlerMissing instead, and one given a second handler with HandlerAlreadySet. A datagram group refuses it with LoopOptionUnsupported too. A group served by HandleLoop without it runs on the zero LoopValue.

<a name="MaxConns"></a>
## func [MaxConns](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func MaxConns(n int) GroupOption
```

MaxConns caps how many connections a group serves at once.

The budget is per group, not per socket: a group listening on a TCP port and a Unix socket, or sharded across several listeners, shares one ceiling — which is what an operator sizing a server actually means. Beyond it a connection is accepted and closed immediately with ConnLimitReached, because a refusal the peer can observe beats a timeout it cannot tell from a hang. Zero means no ceiling.

<a name="MaxHeaderBytes"></a>
## func [MaxHeaderBytes](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func MaxHeaderBytes(n int) GroupOption
```

MaxHeaderBytes caps the bytes net/http reads for a request's line and header fields; a request past the cap is answered 431 Request Header Fields Too Large and never reaches the handler.

Unset (or non-positive) keeps net/http's default of 1 MiB, which applied silently before this option existed. net/http reads a small fixed allowance past the cap before refusing. No effect on a group that does not serve HTTP.

<a name="MaxPacketSize"></a>
## func [MaxPacketSize](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func MaxPacketSize(n int) GroupOption
```

MaxPacketSize caps the datagram size a group accepts.

A larger datagram is dropped and counted in [State](#State).OversizedPackets, never delivered. Truncating would hand the handler a prefix indistinguishable from a complete message, which is a correctness problem rather than a capacity one; a drop it can observe in State is the honest answer.

<a name="Name"></a>
## func [Name](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Name(name string) GroupOption
```

Name names the group in State, logs and errors. On a group declared with an empty name it sets the name, which must then be unique like any other; on one declared with a name it must repeat it. An empty Name, or one that differs from a non-empty declared name, fails Start with GroupNameConflict.

<a name="New"></a>
## func [New](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func New(opts ...Option) *Server
```

New builds a server.

<a name="NewLoopLayer"></a>
## func [NewLoopLayer](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func NewLoopLayer(next LoopHandler) LoopLayer
```

NewLoopLayer returns the LoopLayer a loop middleware's layer embeds over next, forwarding every callback to it.

<a name="Plaintext"></a>
## func [Plaintext](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Plaintext() GroupOption
```

Plaintext declares that the group serves no TLS. Every engine honours it. A group given both Plaintext and TLS, in either order, fails Start with PlaintextWithTLS. It is not yet required of a plaintext group: the simple API will require it of every HTTP group without TLS.

<a name="ReadBufferSize"></a>
## func [ReadBufferSize](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func ReadBufferSize(n int) GroupOption
```

ReadBufferSize sizes the per-connection scratch buffer handed to the handler by Conn.Buffer. It is recycled with the connection, which is what lets a handler read without allocating per connection.

<a name="ReadHeaderTimeout"></a>
## func [ReadHeaderTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func ReadHeaderTimeout(d time.Duration) GroupOption
```

ReadHeaderTimeout bounds the HEADER phase of an HTTP request on its own: the request line and every header field must arrive within d, whatever the read timeout allows a body.

The header phase is the one a slowloris stalls — a byte every few seconds, never finishing a line — and the one an honest client finishes in milliseconds, so it deserves a bound far shorter than a read timeout sized for an upload. A client that stalls there is disconnected at d. Unset (or non-positive) keeps the earlier behaviour: the header phase is bounded by [ReadTimeout](#ReadTimeout). No effect on a group that does not serve HTTP.

<a name="ReadTimeout"></a>
## func [ReadTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func ReadTimeout(d time.Duration) GroupOption
```

ReadTimeout bounds one read from the peer.

It is refreshed per read, not installed once when the connection is accepted: a deadline set at accept time would be a budget for the connection's whole life, which a peer trickling one byte at a time stays comfortably inside. On a group serving an http.Handler it bounds three things: each read of a request body, refreshed before every read — never net/http's own ReadTimeout, which budgets the whole request and would cut off a peer whose every read is inside the bound —, the header phase, unless [ReadHeaderTimeout](#ReadHeaderTimeout) sets it apart, and the wait for the next request when no [IdleTimeout](#IdleTimeout) is set. The time a handler spends between two reads is its own, and the deadline is cleared once the body has ended.

<a name="Shards"></a>
## func [Shards](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func Shards(n int) GroupOption
```

Shards sets how many listeners to open on each of the group's addresses.

Zero selects one per core; one disables sharding. Where the platform (Windows has no SO\_REUSEPORT) or the socket family (a Unix socket) cannot shard, the count collapses to one. An explicit count that collapses is reported in State with the reason; zero collapsing is not, since it asked for nothing a single listener fails to give.

<a name="TLS"></a>
## func [TLS](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func TLS(id tlsid.Identity) GroupOption
```

TLS turns the group's listeners into TLS listeners, or mutual-TLS ones when the identity requires a client certificate.

<a name="WithDrainTimeout"></a>
## func [WithDrainTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func WithDrainTimeout(d time.Duration) Option
```

WithDrainTimeout bounds how long Shutdown waits for in-flight connections before severing them.

<a name="WriteTimeout"></a>
## func [WriteTimeout](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
func WriteTimeout(d time.Duration) GroupOption
```

WriteTimeout bounds one write to the peer, refreshed per write.

<a name="CapabilityValue"></a>
## type [CapabilityValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

```go
type CapabilityValue struct {
	// Name is the capability.
	Name   Capability `json:"name"`
	// Class is "a-kernel", "a-code" or "b".
	Class  string     `json:"class"`
	// Status is "on" (probed and in use), "available" (probed, not asked for),
	// "absent" (probed, the kernel lacks it), "missing" (a class A-code
	// capability the code opted into and the kernel lacks: a fault),
	// "disabled" (switched off by KITSUNIUM_NET_DISABLE or an unknown token,
	// never probed) or "unprobed" (the backend the group runs on has no use for
	// it).
	Status string     `json:"status"`
	// Reason names the probe stage and the kernel's answer, or the switch.
	Reason string     `json:"reason,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="Conn"></a>
## type [Conn](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)


```go
type Conn interface {
	// Buffer returns a connection-scoped scratch buffer sized by the group's
	// read-buffer limit. It is recycled with the connection, which is what lets
	// a handler read without allocating per connection.

	// Group returns the name of the listener group that accepted this
```

```go
}
```

<a name="Group"></a>
## type [Group](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

Group is a set of listeners sharing one handler, middleware chain and policy.

Group.HandleHTTP mounts an http.Handler on the group's listeners: the group keeps its own limits, TLS identity and drain, and net/http only does the protocol.

```go
type Group = svcserver.StreamGroup
```

Group is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/service/net/server.StreamGroup`, declared as:

```go
type Group struct{}
```

<a name="Group.Handle"></a>
### func \(Group\) [Handle](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/stream_group.go>)

```go
func (*Group) Handle(h corenet.ConnHandler) *StreamGroup
```

Handle sets the group's handler. A group declares one handler, once: a second declaration on the same group — Handle, HandleFunc, HandleHTTP or HandleLoop, in any order — does not replace the first, and Start returns HandlerAlreadySet naming the group (ADR 0186 §D1).

<a name="Group.HandleFunc"></a>
### func \(Group\) [HandleFunc](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/stream_group.go>)

```go
func (*Group) HandleFunc(f corenet.ConnHandlerFunc) *StreamGroup
```

HandleFunc sets the group's handler from a plain function. It exists because the overwhelmingly common case is one function, and making that case require a named type would be the papercut that decides whether the API feels light.

<a name="Group.HandleHTTP"></a>
### func \(Group\) [HandleHTTP](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/stream_group.go>)

```go
func (*Group) HandleHTTP(h http.Handler) *StreamGroup
```

HandleHTTP serves an http.Handler over this group's listeners.

The group keeps its own limits, TLS identity and drain; net/http only does the protocol. That split is ADR 0029 D3: reimplementing HTTP would mean owning request smuggling defences, HTTP/2 flow control and HPACK to lose, not gain, throughput.

<a name="Group.HandleLoop"></a>
### func \(Group\) [HandleLoop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/loop_group.go>)

```go
func (*Group) HandleLoop(h corenet.LoopHandler) *StreamGroup
```

HandleLoop serves the group on the loop engine (ADR 0186): h is called on the loop's own thread for every connection of the group, with the bytes each one receives, instead of a goroutine per connection. It is opt-in, and plaintext only.

The group keeps the server's lifecycle — the bind, the adoption of inherited sockets, MaxConns, the drain, State — and Loop(v) sizes and places the engine: io\_uring after a probe of the running kernel, then epoll, on Linux, and the portable backend, the default engine's accept path serialised onto one handler goroutine, everywhere else. Start refuses a loop group given TLS with LoopTLSUnsupported, one given Use or an option neither the engine (IdleTimeout, MaxConns, Adopt, Plaintext, Name, Engine) nor h, through LoopOptionHonourer, honours with LoopOptionUnsupported — an option given counts, its zero value included —, and an explicit backend the platform or the kernel cannot run with UnsupportedPlatform or LoopBackendUnavailable.

A callback of h runs on the loop's thread and must not block it: a blocking call stalls every connection of its loop. h is declared once, like every handler: a second declaration of any kind makes Start return HandlerAlreadySet.

<a name="Group.Use"></a>
### func \(Group\) [Use](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/stream_group.go>)


<a name="Group.UseLoop"></a>
### func \(Group\) [UseLoop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/stream_group.go>)

```go
func (*Group) UseLoop(middlewares ...corenet.Middleware[corenet.LoopHandler]) *StreamGroup
```

UseLoop appends loop middlewares, outermost first, and records the OptionLoopMiddleware kind on every call, even with none. A loop group wraps its handler in them at Start, after checking that each layer is a corenet.LoopLayered whose Next is what it was given and that every one of the eight callbacks, sent through a probe chain, reaches the probe: a layer that fails either check fails Start with LoopMiddlewareInvalid. The chain honours an option when one of its layers or the handler does. A group no loop handler serves refuses UseLoop with LoopOptionUnsupported.

```go
	// Group is the listener group's name.
	Group          string        `json:"group"`
	// Address is the address actually bound, which for a port of zero is the
	// one the kernel chose rather than the one requested.

	// Network is the socket family.

	// Shards is how many listeners were actually opened on this address.

	// Degraded reports that a requested optimisation was unavailable and the
	// server fell back. It is surfaced rather than logged once at startup,
	// because a silent fallback is indistinguishable from a working one and
	// nobody re-reads yesterday's logs to find out.

	// DegradedReason names the fallback in plain words when Degraded is set.

	// Adopted reports a listener inherited from a supervisor rather than bound
	// by this process.
	Adopted        bool          `json:"adopted"`
	// Exclusive reports that no other socket can bind the listener's address
	// while it lives: SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE on Windows, set on a unicast TCP or
	// UDP socket this process binds and read back, never set, on an adopted
	// one. It is false on every other platform, which has no such option.
	Exclusive      bool          `json:"exclusive"`
	// BindWait is how long the bind waited for its address to come free: on
	// Windows, a restarted server's address stays taken until the previous
	// process's connections end, and the bind is retried, bounded. Zero when
	// the first attempt bound.
```

<a name="LoopHandler"></a>
## type [LoopHandler](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

LoopHandler serves the connections of a loop group, one callback per event, on the loop's thread. A callback must not block it.

```go
type LoopHandler = corenet.LoopHandler
```

LoopHandler is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.LoopHandler`, declared as:

```go
type LoopHandler interface {
	// OnBatchEnd is called once per loop iteration, after the OnData calls of
	// every ring of the loop, and before any buffer handed to them returns to the
	// kernel. It is where a handler flushes work it batched — one database
	// commit for every request of the batch, say — before writing the answers.
	OnBatchEnd(io LoopIO)
	// OnClose is called once per connection, last. err is nil when the peer
	// closed cleanly or the handler called Close, and otherwise names why the
	// loop closed it — LoopSpillFull, an idle timeout, the drain, a socket
	// error. ref is stale once OnClose returns.
	OnClose(io LoopIO, ref LoopConnRef, err error)
	// OnData hands the handler the bytes received on ref and returns how many of
	// them it consumed, from 0 to len(buf). buf stays valid until the next
	// OnBatchEnd returns, never later, and the handler must not write to it.
	// The unconsumed tail is kept in the connection's spill and handed back
	// first, followed by the next bytes, on the next OnData; a tail past the
	// spill ceiling closes the connection with LoopSpillFull. A value outside
	// 0 to len(buf) is treated as len(buf).
	OnData(io LoopIO, ref LoopConnRef, buf []byte) int
	// OnOpen is called once per accepted connection, before any OnData for it.
	// Pressure(ref) already answers for this connection.
	OnOpen(io LoopIO, ref LoopConnRef)
	// OnTimeout is called when the deadline set by SetDeadline on ref expires.
	// The connection stays open: closing it is the handler's choice.
	OnTimeout(io LoopIO, ref LoopConnRef)
	// OnWritable is called when ref's pending output falls below the loop's
	// low-water mark after a Write was refused with LoopOutputFull or left output
	// pending past the mark, so a producer that paused can resume.
	OnWritable(io LoopIO, ref LoopConnRef)
}
```

```go

```

OnBatchEnd is called once per loop iteration, after the OnData calls of every ring of the loop, and before any buffer handed to them returns to the kernel. It is where a handler flushes work it batched — one database commit for every request of the batch, say — before writing the answers.

The unconsumed tail is kept in the connection's spill and handed back first, followed by the next bytes, on the next OnData; a tail past the spill ceiling closes the connection with LoopSpillFull. A value outside 0 to len(buf) is treated as len(buf).

<a name="LoopIO"></a>
## type [LoopIO](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

LoopIO is what a loop offers its handler: Write, Close, SetDeadline and Pressure on its connections, from a callback, and Post from any goroutine.

```go
type LoopIO = corenet.LoopIO
```

LoopIO is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.LoopIO`, declared as:

```go
type LoopIO interface {
	// Close closes ref's connection once the output already written has left,
	// and calls OnClose. A second Close, or a Close on a stale reference, returns
	// LoopStaleRef and does nothing.
	Close(ref LoopConnRef) error
	// Loop returns the index of the loop this LoopIO belongs to, from 0 to the
	// group's lane count less one, fixed for the loop's life: its lane. A
	// handler keeps its per-lane state — a scratch, a batch, a buffer — in a
	// slice indexed by it and sized at LoopStarter.OnStart, so a callback finds
	// its own with no lock and no map. The portable backend runs LoopValue.Loops
	// lanes too, one handler goroutine each. Any goroutine may call it.
	Loop() int
	// Post queues op to run once on the loop's thread with arg, and wakes the
	// loop. It is the one operation any goroutine may call. The queue is
	// preallocated and holds no closure: op is a plain function and arg an
	// integer the caller gives meaning to. Each posted operation runs exactly
	// once, in the order posted; a full queue refuses with LoopPostQueueFull, and
	// a loop that has stopped with ServerClosed.
	Post(op PostFunc, arg uintptr) error
	// Pressure reports whether ref's connection was accepted, or has since come,
	// under the loop's soft pressure: the group serves more connections than its
	// soft bound. It is a primitive; what a protocol makes of it — HTTP/1.1
	// answers Connection: close — is the protocol adapter's. A stale reference
	// reports false.
	Pressure(ref LoopConnRef) bool
	// SetDeadline arms ref's timer to fire OnTimeout after d, on the loop's
	// coarse timer wheel: it fires no earlier than d and at most one wheel tick
	// late. A d of zero or less disarms it. Arming again replaces the previous
	// deadline.
	SetDeadline(ref LoopConnRef, d time.Duration) error
	// Write copies p into ref's output and returns. Writes on one reference leave
	// in the order they were made, and p may be reused once Write returns. It is
	// refused with LoopOutputFull, copying nothing, when p would pass the
	// connection's output ceiling or the loop's global output budget, and with
	// LoopStaleRef when ref's connection has closed.
	Write(ref LoopConnRef, p []byte) error
}
```

<a name="LoopIO.Close"></a>
### func \(LoopIO\) [Close](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/gen_ports.go>)

```go

```

Close closes ref's connection once the output already written has left, and calls OnClose. A second Close, or a Close on a stale reference, returns LoopStaleRef and does nothing.

<a name="LoopIO.Loop"></a>
### func \(LoopIO\) [Loop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/gen_ports.go>)

```go
func (LoopIO) Loop() int
```

Loop returns the index of the loop this LoopIO belongs to, from 0 to the group's lane count less one, fixed for the loop's life: its lane. A handler keeps its per-lane state — a scratch, a batch, a buffer — in a slice indexed by it and sized at LoopStarter.OnStart, so a callback finds its own with no lock and no map. The portable backend runs LoopValue.Loops lanes too, one handler goroutine each. Any goroutine may call it.

<a name="LoopIO.Post"></a>

```go
func (LoopIO) Post(op PostFunc, arg uintptr) error
```

Post queues op to run once on the loop's thread with arg, and wakes the loop. It is the one operation any goroutine may call. The queue is preallocated and holds no closure: op is a plain function and arg an integer the caller gives meaning to. Each posted operation runs exactly once, in the order posted; a full queue refuses with LoopPostQueueFull, and a loop that has stopped with ServerClosed.

<a name="LoopIO.Pressure"></a>
### func \(LoopIO\) [Pressure](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/gen_ports.go>)

```go

```

Pressure reports whether ref's connection was accepted, or has since come, under the loop's soft pressure: the group serves more connections than its soft bound. It is a primitive; what a protocol makes of it — HTTP/1.1 answers Connection: close — is the protocol adapter's. A stale reference reports false.

<a name="LoopIO.SetDeadline"></a>
### func \(LoopIO\) [SetDeadline](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/gen_ports.go>)

```go

```

SetDeadline arms ref's timer to fire OnTimeout after d, on the loop's coarse timer wheel: it fires no earlier than d and at most one wheel tick late. A d of zero or less disarms it. Arming again replaces the previous deadline.

<a name="LoopIO.Write"></a>

```go

```

Write copies p into ref's output and returns. Writes on one reference leave in the order they were made, and p may be reused once Write returns. It is refused with LoopOutputFull, copying nothing, when p would pass the connection's output ceiling or the loop's global output budget, and with LoopStaleRef when ref's connection has closed.

<a name="LoopValue"></a>
## type [LoopValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

LoopValue configures a group's loop engine, passed by Loop. Every field is optional: zero selects the domain default.

```go
type LoopValue = corenet.LoopValue
```

LoopValue is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.LoopValue`, declared as:

```go
type LoopValue struct {
	// Backend is the mechanic to run on. LoopBackendAuto takes the best one the
	// platform's probe reaches and reports any fallback in State; an explicit
	// backend the platform cannot run is refused at Start.
	Backend      LoopBackend   `json:"backend"`
	// Loops is the number of loops, each one goroutine locked to its OS thread
	// on a native backend. Zero selects one. The SDK never sets GOMAXPROCS:
	// sizing the process against its loops is the consumer's policy, and State
	// reports both.
	Loops        int           `json:"loops"`
	// Rings is the number of descriptor shards inside one loop, each with its
	// own table of at most min(RLIMIT_NOFILE, IORING_MAX_FIXED_FILES) entries:
	// what lets io_uring serve more connections than RLIMIT_NOFILE. Zero
	// derives it, ⌈max(MaxConns, SoftConns) / min(RLIMIT_NOFILE,
	// IORING_MAX_FIXED_FILES)⌉, and one when both are zero; that is the only
	// formula, and State says where the value came from. epoll and the portable
	// backend run one ring whatever it says.
	Rings        int           `json:"rings"`
	// CQBatch bounds the completions or events one loop iteration reaps before
	// it calls OnBatchEnd. Zero selects the domain default.
	CQBatch      int           `json:"cq_batch"`
	// SpillCap is the most unconsumed input, in bytes, one connection may hold
	// between OnData calls. Past it the connection is closed with
	// LoopSpillFull. Zero selects the domain default.
	SpillCap     int           `json:"spill_cap"`
	// OutputCap is the most written and unsent output, in bytes, one
	// connection may hold. A Write past it is refused with LoopOutputFull. Zero
	// selects the domain default.
	OutputCap    int           `json:"output_cap"`
	// SoftConns is the soft connection bound: a connection accepted while the
	// group serves more is flagged under pressure (LoopIO.Pressure), so a
	// protocol can ask its peer to leave. It refuses nothing; MaxConns does.
	// Zero sets no soft bound.
	SoftConns    int           `json:"soft_conns"`
	// EvictIdle is how long a connection must have been idle before the loop
	// may close it to admit another under hard pressure — the process out of
	// descriptors, or MaxConns reached. A connection with unread bytes is
	// never evicted. Zero evicts nothing.
	EvictIdle    DurationValue `json:"evict_idle"`
	// Capabilities opts the group into kernel capabilities of class A-code
	// (ADR 0189). Each is probed and used where the kernel has it, reported
	// "missing" and as a fault where it does not, and never used once
	// KITSUNIUM_NET_DISABLE names it. An engine, a class B capability or an
	// unknown token is refused at Start with LoopCapabilityRefused. Nil asks
	// for none; the class A-kernel capabilities need no opt-in.
	Capabilities []Capability  `json:"capabilities,omitempty"`
}
```

<a name="Server.Close"></a>
### func \(Server\) [Close](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/lifecycle.go>)

```go
func (*Server) Close() error
```

Close releases every listener and severs every live connection immediately, without draining.

<a name="Server.Group"></a>
### func \(Server\) [Group](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/server.go>)

```go
func (*Server) Group(name string, opts ...GroupOption) *StreamGroup
```

Group declares a listener group and returns it for handler attachment.

It returns the group rather than (group, error) on purpose: a declaration error is recorded and surfaced by Start, so the common path stays a single chained expression instead of an error check per line.

<a name="Server.PacketGroup"></a>
### func \(Server\) [PacketGroup](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/server.go>)

```go

```

PacketGroup declares a datagram listener group and returns it for handler attachment. It mirrors Group deliberately: the point of the domain is that a UDP service is declared the same way a TCP one is.

<a name="Server.RegisterHealth"></a>
### func \(Server\) [RegisterHealth](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/health.go>)

```go
func (*Server) RegisterHealth(h corehealth.Health) error
```

RegisterHealth registers the server's readiness and liveness checks on h, both named "net/server" (ADR 0188). Readiness is built from State: ready while serving with no stalled loop group. Liveness fails once a loop group has stayed stalled for the stall grace, 30 seconds. A receive that never completes on a live ring is not watched.

<a name="Server.Serve"></a>
### func \(Server\) [Serve](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/lifecycle.go>)

```go
func (*Server) Serve(ctx context.Context) error
```

Serve starts the server and blocks until ctx is cancelled, then drains.

It is the one-call entry point: a caller that has nothing else to do on the main goroutine writes Serve and gets startup, blocking and graceful shutdown without assembling them. It also returns, after the same drain, once every ring of a loop group has been drained by its watchdog: LoopGroupStalled, naming the group (ADR 0188).

<a name="Server.Shutdown"></a>
### func \(Server\) [Shutdown](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/lifecycle.go>)

```go
func (*Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error
```

Shutdown stops accepting and waits for in-flight connections to finish, severing what remains once ctx expires.

<a name="Server.Start"></a>
### func \(Server\) [Start](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/service/net/server/lifecycle.go>)

```go
func (*Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error
```

Start binds every group's listeners and begins accepting.

It returns once every listener is bound, so a caller that gets a nil error knows the ports are open — which is what makes a test able to dial immediately, and a supervisor able to report readiness honestly.

```go
func (*Server) State() corenet.StateValue
```

State returns a snapshot of the server's lifecycle and listeners.

<a name="State"></a>
## type [State](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/net/server/gen_facade.go>)

State is a snapshot of the server's lifecycle and listeners.

```go
type State = corenet.StateValue
```

State is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/core/net.StateValue`, declared as:

```go
type State struct {
	// Phase is where the server sits in its lifecycle.
	Phase            Phase                `json:"phase"`
	// Listeners describes every bound listener, including any degradation.
	Listeners        []ListenerStateValue `json:"listeners"`
	// ActiveConns is the number of connections currently being served.
	ActiveConns      int64                `json:"active_conns"`
	// TotalConns is the number accepted since the server started.
	TotalConns       uint64               `json:"total_conns"`
	// RejectedConns is the number turned away by the connection ceiling.
	RejectedConns    uint64               `json:"rejected_conns"`
	// OversizedPackets is the number of datagrams dropped for passing their
	// group's MaxPacketSize. They are counted rather than delivered because the
	// kernel has already discarded the tail, and the prefix that survives is
	// indistinguishable from a complete message to the handler receiving it. A
	// read loop has nobody to return an error to, so this counter is the report.
	OversizedPackets uint64               `json:"oversized_packets"`
	// AcceptBackoffs is the number of times an accept loop waited after Accept
	// failed with anything but its listener closing — the process out of file
	// descriptors, typically, with connections still queued. Retrying at once
	// would spin a core per listener while the condition lasts; each wait is
	// 5 ms, doubling to 1 s, and the next accepted connection starts the curve
	// over. A count that keeps rising is a server that cannot accept.
	AcceptBackoffs   uint64               `json:"accept_backoffs"`
	// Loops reports every loop group (ADR 0186 §D8). It is empty while the
	// server serves none.
	Loops            []LoopStateValue     `json:"loops,omitempty"`
	// Override reports what KITSUNIUM_NET_ENGINE and KITSUNIUM_NET_DISABLE did
	// (ADR 0188).
	Override         OverrideValue        `json:"override"`
	// Faults lists everything the server runs without now, the degradations of
	// Listeners and Loops included; Degraded is true when it is not empty.
	Faults           []FaultValue         `json:"faults,omitempty"`
	// Fallbacks counts the engine fallbacks and keeps the last one.
	Fallbacks        FallbacksValue       `json:"fallbacks"`
	// Platform names the operating system, its release and the toolchain.
	Platform         PlatformValue        `json:"platform"`
}
```

<a name="State.Degraded"></a>
### func \(State\) [Degraded](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/core/net/state.go>)

```go
func (State) Degraded() bool
```

Degraded reports whether the server runs with any fault — a listener or loop group that fell back from a requested optimisation, a drained ring, a stalled loop group, an unknown environment token — so a caller can assert "no silent degradation" in one call. It reads Faults, and still the Degraded flags of Listeners and Loops for a value built by hand (ADR 0188).
